notes: The 1962 volume of the Recreation and Park Commission. Curated: design approvals, dedications and names. By 1962 building contracts went through the Department of Public Works, so few contracts appear.

coverage.remaining: Routine items not curated. Held: George A. Applegarth's alteration plans for the Senior Center in the Aquatic Park building (Mar 29 and Dec 6), no Aquatic Park page; Storyland exhibits by J. Francis Ward, the Conservatory catwalk and the Palace of Fine Arts plan not curated.
coverage.note: Read by passage with scan2.py; dated by slash footers. Curated list F1962.py.

findings.address_as_written: Edward P. Garrigan Field at Funston Playground
findings.description: The Commission received a letter of thanks from the Garrigan family for the dedication of the Edward P. Garrigan Field, the baseball diamond at Funston Playground, whose plaque the Commission had approved in February (Resolution 4706), subject to the Art Commission.

citation.label: Minutes of the Recreation and Park Commission, June 14, 1962

findings.description: The Recreation and Park Commission approved the plans, elevations and estimated cost, about $152,000, of a neighborhood playground with a clubhouse near Hahn Street and Visitacion Avenue, presented for Hans U. Gerson of William Gladstone Merchant & Associates, the architects engaged in April (Resolution 4799) through the Department of Public Works; it was paid for from the 1955 playground bond fund.

findings.address_as_written: Queen Wilhelmina Gardens, Golden Gate Park
findings.description: The Recreation and Park Commission named the tulip garden east of the old North Dutch Windmill The Queen Wilhelmina Garden, as a tribute to the late Queen of the Netherlands and in thanks to the people of Holland, whose gifts of tulip bulbs had made the garden possible.
